description: InterWeave's rules for runtime/github/arm.sh. boundary.paths is InterWeave CLAUDE.md's security-boundary list — identity and key handling, trust policy, wire or configuration parsing, persistence, admission and resource accounting, and anything cryptographic — in path form, matched case-insensitively. Whole trees where the tree is the boundary: the wire contracts and the normative configuration schema and examples (architecture/contracts/, architecture/config/ — a schema is the wire: #171 flipped one with no crate touched, and profile-config takes its ranges from config.schema.yaml); identity; every api/ contract crate; config parsing; discovery (peer-cache persistence, query budgets, untrusted peer and address input); the local IPC server and client; the transport stack; the human chat protocol, store, transport client and core (retention decides what content is durable); the two transport apps; the vendored third_party/ code; the normative vectors under fixtures/ (identity derivation, IPC framing — a fixture changes only with its contract); the root Cargo.toml, whose [patch.crates-io] points crates at third_party/ (the store caps ADR-0053 requires live there), so every root manifest change is reviewed (InterWeave #177 review, F1); and .cargo/config(.toml) at any depth — Cargo reads it from every ancestor of the directory it runs in — where it honours the same [patch], [source] replace-with and paths overrides (agent-fabric #90 review). Words where the boundary is a file anywhere: key, identity, seed, mnemonic, bip39, ed25519, secret, trust, crypt, sign, noise, tls, cipher, parse, codec, wire, protocol, persist, store, admission, quota, accounting, limit. Over-matching costs a review; under-matching costs a boundary. boundary.exempt is dropped first: Markdown and architecture/ prose outside the contracts and the config, tools/, xtask/, .github/, .claude/ and .agent-fabric/ — documentation and mechanical changes are not on the list. A .cargo/config(.toml) is never exempt, at any depth and in any letter case, under tools/ and xtask/ too. deny.toml, the dependency policy check_dependencies.sh and the advisory check enforce, is on it: an edit can loosen the supply chain (a git source allowed, an advisory ignored), and it changes rarely. Cargo.lock is not: it changes in almost every feature PR, and those checks already hold it to deny.toml. The Claude channel (crates/claude/, apps/claude-channel/) is on it before its code lands: it will parse a wire protocol and decide what a local process may send. crates/human/client-api/ is not: types only, no I/O, store or keys. The owner ruled these four on 2026-10-04. No classes: InterWeave arms under eight work commits only on the owner's word (CLAUDE.md §9). Declared by devex-tooling. waiver_role: a --no-boundary waiver is a DECISION or REPLY from a login holding architect-cto, sent TO the arming session, carrying WAIVES: <owner/repo>#<n>@<head sha> (the owner's ruling, 2026-10-04: the waiver moves from the owner's approval to architect-cto's).

changes.2026-10-04 nested .cargo/config: Cargo reads .cargo/config.toml from every ancestor of where it runs, so a nested one can redirect crates as the root's can; widened at any depth (#90 re-review risk; devex-tooling, 6e49aa67)
changes.2026-10-04 deny.toml and the Claude chan: the owner's ruling on InterWeave #177's open paths: deny.toml, crates/claude/ and apps/claude-channel/ on; Cargo.lock and crates/human/client-api/ off (devex-tooling, e96860c)
changes.2026-10-04 .cargo/config under an exempt: the exemption ran first, so tools/**/.cargo/config(.toml) and xtask/.cargo/config escaped the at-any-depth pattern; a .cargo/config is never exempt now (#91 review thread, coordinator relay seq 11599; devex-tooling)
changes.2026-10-04 .cargo/config case-insensitiv: exempt is matched case-sensitively and paths is not, so tools/foo/.Cargo/config.toml stayed exempt though a case-insensitive filesystem lets Cargo read it; the never-exempt lookahead is case-insensitive now (#91 re-review P3, coordinator message 01a105f7-f012-7dee-8567-2a7a6397ce7b; devex-tooling)
